name: scheduler
purpose: Show and edit events in day, week, work-week, month, agenda, and resource timeline views (SPEC section 18.19 Scheduler, Calendar Scheduler, Timeline Scheduler): recurring series with exceptions, timezone-aware wall-clock layout, business hours and holidays from a Business Calendar definition, pointer and keyboard editing with recurring scopes and undo, and events from memory or a range data source (loadEvents).
whenToUse: Team calendars, room or equipment booking, shift or appointment planning.
Resource planning where rows are people, rooms, or machines (timeline view).
Any calendar where events repeat and timezones and DST must be exact.
whenNotToUse: Project plans with dependencies: use Gantt.
Picking a date: use Date Picker; picking a time range: Schedule Picker.
Tens of thousands of events in one visible range: aggregate on the server first.
responsive: The toolbar wraps. Grids scroll in two dimensions inside the body (WCAG 1.4.10 allows two-dimensional scrolling for data grids): day columns keep at least 6rem, timeline columns 3rem, month cells 6rem; row headers and column headers stay sticky. Views can be limited with `views` for narrow layouts (agenda reads well at 320 px).
rtl: The direction option mirrors columns, timeline time flow, chevrons, and Left/Right keys (Shift+Left/Right resizing follows the reading direction).
theme: Events use the chart palette (color 1..8, from the event, else its resource) as a left bar and an 18 % tint over the surface with body text; non-working time uses the sunken surface; holidays use the warning foreground; the current time is a line in the error foreground. Forced colors: events are outlined in CanvasText, non-working time is hatched, selection uses Highlight. The recurring-scope prompt uses Dialog (import dialog and button styles).
timezone: Every view is laid out in the configured timezone (UTC unless configured, section 8.1): timed events are Instants positioned by their wall-clock time in that zone; all-day events are PlainDate (inclusive last day). Series expand in the event's timeZone (default the scheduler zone), so a 09:00 series stays at 09:00 across DST; slots in a DST gap resolve with the disambiguation policy (compatible by default). Moves keep the real duration and the wall-clock time on the target day.
security: Titles, locations, and descriptions are rendered with textContent; renderEvent content is the application's. No HTML parsing; CSP-safe (custom properties through the CSSOM).
dataHandling: No persistence or telemetry. loadEvents is called per visible range with an AbortSignal (superseded ranges are aborted, requestTimeoutMs times out), answers are validated (SCHEDULER_DATA_SOURCE) and cached per range until an edit or refresh(). Edits are emitted as the cancelable aui-event-change with the changes and every event; call undo() or update({ events }) to roll back after a failed save.

budgets.budget: < 120 ms in headless Chromium (e2e performance test)

budgets.metric: Next period, month view with 1,000 events (200 recurring)
budgets.budget: < 120 ms in headless Chromium (e2e performance test)

budgets.metric: Timeline with 500 resources and 2,000 events, create
budgets.budget: < 150 ms in headless Chromium (e2e performance test)

performance.testedScale: Up to 1,000 occurrences in a visible range and 500 timeline resources (rows are virtualized above 60 resources). Series are expanded per visible range, fast-forwarded without COUNT.

limitations: Multi-day timed events appear as one segment per day in time views (not in the all-day row).
All-day and timed events do not convert by dragging between the all-day row and the time grid.
The timeline shows one day (slots), one week, or one month (days); no custom zoom levels.
Month cells show monthEventLimit rows and "+N more" (which opens the day view).
Deleting only emits aui-event-delete; the application removes the event.
No drag and drop from outside the scheduler, no event creation UI (aui-slot-activate asks the application).
Recurrence follows the RRULE subset of @absoluteui/core.
Screen-reader behavior has not yet been manually verified with NVDA, JAWS, and VoiceOver.
unsupported: Rendering HTML in titles or locations.
Events without an end, negative durations.
antiPatterns: Sending local wall-clock strings to the server instead of Instants and a timeZone.
Re-creating the scheduler on every change instead of update({ events }).
Interactive elements inside renderEvent content (the event is already a button).

adapters.react: @absoluteui/react/scheduler: AuiScheduler component with props for every option and on* callbacks for events.
